Tensor networks and quantum information

Song Cheng.

Associate Professor, Quantum Symmetry Group

Beijing Institute of Mathematical Sciences and Applications

I study the connections between quantum many-body physics, quantum computing, and machine learning through the language of tensor networks.

Quantum Symmetry Group · BIMSADirections of interest↓

Research

Many structures, one language.

Learning representation

Tensor-network approaches to generative modeling, supervised learning, and the compression of deep neural networks.

Quantum simulation

Classical simulation of noisy quantum circuits and quantum dynamics, with an emphasis on operator complexity and error mitigation.

Topology
& quantum codes

The structure of topological quantum states and quantum error-correcting codes, explored through tensor networks and diagrammatic methods.

Watch

Tensor networks in a nutshell.

We’re hiring

Postdoctoral positions in tensor networks and quantum information

The Quantum Symmetry Group at BIMSA is looking for postdoctoral researchers who want to take tensor network methods into quantum computing, quantum error correction and machine learning.

Application link↗BIMSA postdoc positions↗

How to apply

Apply online through MathJobs with:

  • Cover letter
  • Curriculum vitae
  • Research statement
  • Publication list with links
  • Three reference letters, submitted by the referees

Questions are welcome at chengsong@bimsa.cn.

Research directions
  • Tensor network algorithms for quantum many-body systems
  • Classical simulation of noisy quantum circuits
  • Tensor networks, topological order and quantum codes
  • Tensor networks for machine learning
Terms
  • Two-year appointment, with a possible one-year extension upon evaluation
  • RMB 300k–500k per year (about USD 42k–70k), depending on qualifications
  • Subsidized housing and health insurance
  • Generous travel grants
Who we look for
A PhD in physics, mathematics, computer science or a related field, completed before the appointment begins. Experience with tensor networks, quantum information or numerical methods is welcome; curiosity matters more than a checklist.
